Grade: PP1
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PERFORMANCE
Topic 9.1: musical Rhymes

Close your notes and say aloud: what musical Rhymes is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “musical Rhymes” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: demonstrate the ability to recite rhyming simple rhymes for fun • Guide learners to rhyme in)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to musical Rhymes in your own words. (skill: Appreciate different rhymes pairs or small groups • Guide learners to present own composed rhymes)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: Perform simple singing games. games for fun • Guide learners to perform)

Example 4: Show how “musical Rhymes” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: Perform simple singing singing games from different games using props cultures in groups and in pairs)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach musical Rhymes to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate the ability to recite rhyming simple rhymes for fun • Guide learners to rhyme in.
3. Practise this skill: Appreciate different rhymes pairs or small groups • Guide learners to present own composed rhymes.
4. Practise this skill: Perform simple singing games. games for fun • Guide learners to perform.
5. Make one local Kenya example of musical Rhymes from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for musical Rhymes: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study musical Rhymes?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which rhyme do you Rhymes learner should be able to; listen to recorded rhymes recite?
2. Which singing games games leaner should be able to; singing games freely. do you enjoy most?
3. Which costumes do 5 Lessons for enjoyment you use?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what musical Rhymes means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate the ability to recite rhyming simple rhymes for fun • Guide learners to rhyme in.
5. Be able to: Appreciate different rhymes pairs or small groups • Guide learners to present own composed rhymes.
